notes.headline: This mix is clipping at +3.0 dBTP and squashed to -1.2 LUFS — pull the mix bus limiting off and rebounce with real headroom before it goes to mastering.
notes.summary: Everything here comes from one cause: something on your mix bus is pushing the whole thing into the ceiling. True peak is +3.0 dBTP, integrated loudness is -1.2 LUFS, and peak-to-loudness is down to 4.2 dB, which means transients are being flattened. For a mix headed to mastering none of that helps you — it just removes the room a mastering engineer needs to work. Bypass the limiter, trim the master fader back, and the technical score goes from 8.3 to 10 without touching a single balance.

priorities.title: Clipped, over-limited mix bus
priorities.why: At +3.0 dBTP you'll hear distortion on playback and worse after lossy encoding, and at -1.2 LUFS Spotify would turn it down about 12.8 dB anyway, so the loudness buys you nothing. The 4.2 dB peak-to-loudness ratio shows the limiter is eating your transients. A mix going to mastering should arrive with headroom, not volume.

priorities.title: Little contrast between sections
priorities.why: Loudness range is 2.7 LU, so verses and choruses sit at nearly the same level. Some of this will come back on its own once the limiting is off, but arrangement-level moves will make the song breathe.

listen_for: After bypassing the limiter and trimming, watch the meters through the loudest section — peaks should land around −6 to −3 dBFS with nothing touching full scale.
Drum hits and any percussive transients: they should have attack and snap back rather than sounding pinned flat.
Play the verse into the chorus and check you can hear a lift of a couple of dB without reaching for the fader.
Check the bounce on headphones or earbuds for the crackle and grit that clipping leaves behind, especially on sustained loud passages.
strengths: Left/right balance is dead centre at -0.01 dB — nothing is pulling to one side.
Stereo correlation at 0.744 is healthy, and the low end holds together at 0.768.
Mono fold-down only costs 0.63 dB, so this will translate fine on single-speaker playback.

judge.priority_order: Critical F1 is grouped first with F2/F3 (all tied to the limiter/clipping cause) and info-level F4 follows, matching severity order in the report.
judge.explains_impact: Each priority ties the numbers to audible effects (‘you'll hear distortion,’ ‘Spotify would turn it down,’ ‘verses and choruses sit at nearly the same level’).
judge.groups_causes: F1, F2, F3 are correctly merged under one root cause (mix-bus limiting), consistent with the report's shared fix steps (F1.2/F2.1 bypass limiter), while F4 is kept separate as an unrelated arrangement issue.
judge.specific: Notes cite exact figures from the report (+3.0 dBTP, -1.2 LUFS, 4.2 dB PLR, 2.7 LU LRA, 0.744 correlation, 0.63 dB mono loss) rather than generic advice.
judge.stage_appropriate: Notes correctly frame the fix as restoring headroom for mastering ('arrive with headroom, not volume') rather than judging loudness against release standards.
judge.faithful: All claims (score 8.3→10, PLR 4.2 dB indicating limiting, LUFS -1.2 turn-down of ~12.8 dB, correlation/mono figures) match the report without adding unsupported claims.
judge.concise: Despite covering all findings, the notes stay focused and avoid filler or repetition beyond what's needed to explain cause and impact.
